items.title: Daniel Ricciardo opens door to racing return with Max Verstappen at Le Mans
items.summary: Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo has revealed he would consider a one-off appearance at the Le Mans 24 Hours and named his former Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen as his first choice to share a car with.

items.title: Daniel Ricciardo reveals major regret over 2018 Red Bull departure
items.summary: Daniel Ricciardo has admitted he wishes he had stayed at the Red Bull Formula 1 team rather than leaving at the end of the 2018 season. The Australian won seven grands prix with Red Bull, but shocked everyone when he left the team and joined Renault for 2019, leaving Max Verstappen as the team’s undisputed lead driver.

items.title: FIA to use AI to help shape future F1 regulations in new AWS partnership
items.summary: The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) will use artificial intelligence from Amazon Web Services (AWS) to help draw up the rules for Formula 1's next era of cars, after signing a new global partnership with the tech giant.

items.title: Christian Horner addresses past misconduct allegations in new interview
items.summary: The allegations surrounding Christian Horner's final months at Red Bull Racing still draw questions from fans despite him being cleared of any wrongdoing. Now, 15 months after his exit from the team, Horner has finally broken his silence on that time. Sitting down with 60 Minutes Australia, the former team principal addressed the allegations with uncompromising defiance.

items.title: Christian Horner reveals details of Red Bull exit in emotional interview
items.summary: Ever since Red Bull unceremoniously dropped Christian Horner on 9 July 2025, the Formula 1 paddock has been buzzing with endless speculation about what actually triggered the guillotine. Was it the early-2024 allegations? Was it the fact that Red Bull only managed to win two grand prix races in the first half of 2025? Or was it Max Verstappen’s camp finally forcing a hard ultimatum?

items.title: Five things to look out for at the F1 Mexico GP
items.summary: Formula 1 is back again this weekend with the highly popular Mexico Grand Prix, which comes just seven days after Kimi Antonelli romped to victory in Austin. That was the Mercedes driver’s ninth win of the 2026 season after dominating from pole in a race largely defined by strategy with Antonelli nailing a one-stopper.

items.title: Max Verstappen sits out for Red Bull in Mexico GP FP1
items.summary: Max Verstappen will step aside during first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix as Red Bull continues to complete its quota of rookie runs in FP1 sessions.

items.title: F1 publishes first Social Impact Report; key student scholarship renewed
items.summary: Formula 1 has published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, with over half a million young people across the world having beneffited from F1 programmes last year. In initiatives designed to educate, inspire and open pathways into the sport in 2025, youngsters from across 71 countries were able to take a step closer to F1.

items.title: Sergio Perez signs fresh Cadillac F1 deal until 2029
items.summary: Sergio Perez has committed to the Cadillac F1 project until at least 2029 as the Mexican signed fresh terms with the US-owned outfit. Perez joined F1's expansion team for its 2026 debut after his Red Bull exit left him on the sidelines last year.

items.title: Oliver Bearman explains why Haas’ 2026 F1 car is ‘hitting its ceiling’
items.summary: Oliver Bearman believes Haas cannot extract much more performance from its 2026 Formula 1 car, following the United States Grand Prix. Bearman displayed encouraging Friday pace at the Circuit of The Americas, with 11th and 10th in the opening two free practice sessions, before slipping down the order – to the extent that he qualified just 16th.

items.title: Yet another DNF for Cadillac’s Valtteri Bottas: ‘Sometimes we don’t quite understand it’
items.summary: Valtteri Bottas described the Cadillac Formula 1 team as struggling to understand its issues, after he retired from Sunday’s United States Grand Prix. Bottas suffered his ninth retirement of the season at the Circuit of The Americas, a surprisingly high number for a driver whose pre-2026 DNF rate was 11%.

items.title: Why Aston Martin and Red Bull were asked about an unlikely F1 engine partnership
items.summary: One of the most remarkable moments on Sunday in Austin did not take place on the track itself, but rather in the Formula 1 paddock after the US Grand Prix. During the usual post-race media sessions, both Aston Martin and Red Bull’s representatives were asked about a subject that had very little to do with the race at the Circuit of the Americas – quite the opposite, in fact.

items.title: Audi F1 power unit division brings back CEO role
items.summary: Audi has announced Thomas Fuhr will become CEO of Audi Formula Racing GmbH, the Neuburg-based division developing its F1 power units. Fuhr will sit at the head of the Neuburg plant as an addition to the current team, which Audi says will allow chief technical director Stefan Dreyer to "focus fully on leading the technical development of Audi’s Formula 1 power unit".

items.title: FIA partners with AWS to help drive future F1 regulations
items.summary: The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities. AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations.

items.title: Max Verstappen admits Red Bull was “just a little average” in Austin
items.summary: Despite finishing on the podium, Max Verstappen was disappointed after the United States Grand Prix. Talking after the race, the Dutchman said his Red Bull team was "just a little average" as he faced the wrong tyre choice, power unit problems as well as radio issues.

items.title: Toto Wolff reveals how Williams' surprise victory helped him secure Mercedes role
items.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff revealed a jibe at Pastor Maldonado that helped him get his place on the team, as the Austrian businessman gave a comparison between the star Mercedes drivers and the then-Williams driver. Wolff was a shareholder and executive at Williams in 2012, when Maldonado took a surprising victory in the Spanish Grand Prix.

items.title: George Russell F1 title chances defended by Toto Wolff after Helmut Marko comments
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 team chief Toto Wolff has rejected former Red Bull motorsport adviser Helmut Marko's claim that George Russell will never get another shot at the F1 title. Russell currently sits 123 points behind his team-mate and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers' standings.

items.title: Helmut Marko invests in AI start-up after Red Bull F1 exit
items.summary: Former Red Bull motorsport adviser Helmut Marko has become an investor in an Austrian artificial intelligence start-up that lets people leave personal messages to be delivered to loved ones after they die.

items.title: Red Bull responds to Aston Martin F1 power unit rumours
items.summary: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has confirmed that the team is not in "serious conversations" when it comes to supplying another Formula 1 team with power units. This includes Aston Martin. The Silverstone-based team has struggled with its power unit performance all season as its works partnership with Honda has been strained.

items.title: Toto Wolff takes blame for George Russell's US GP struggles
items.summary: If you looked at the two sides of the Mercedes garage after Sunday's United States Grand Prix, you would assume they were running completely different machinery. On one side, sensation Andrea Kimi Antonelli was celebrating a miraculous, dominant race victory.

items.title: Valtteri Bottas denies he might lose his Cadillac seat for F1 2027
items.summary: Valtteri Bottas insists Cadillac is happy with him and his contract is “all OK” for 2027, amid recent rumours about his Formula 1 future. Bottas’ recent lack of both qualifying and race pace has led to speculation on the driver market.

items.title: Franco Colapinto, George Russell to sit out FP1 at F1 Mexico GP
items.summary: Gabriele Mini is set to make his Formula 1 race weekend debut, driving Franco Colapinto’s Alpine in Free Practice 1 at the Mexico Grand Prix.

items.title: The mistakes that cost Lewis Hamilton a podium at F1’s US GP
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why the podium narrowly eluded him in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix. The Ferrari driver started from fifth on the grid and jumped Isack Hadjar for fourth at lights out, despite being the only driver on used (soft) tyres for the opening stint.

items.title: McLaren boss claims the MCL40 had podium pace despite a “disappointing” P5 and P7
items.summary: In modern Formula 1, raw race pace means absolutely nothing if you completely bottle your qualifying laps on Saturday afternoon. Without track position, you are simply burning up your tyres in dirty air while the race leaders cruise off into the distance. That is the reality McLaren faced at the United States Grand Prix.

items.title: “I couldn’t disappear” – Oliver Bearman rues “crazy” penalty for Pierre Gasly clash
items.summary: Oliver Bearman says he was “pretty shocked” to land a 10-second penalty for his collision with Pierre Gasly in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix. Bearman gained two spots on the opening lap of the Austin race and made a move on 10th-placed Gasly on the next tour, down the inside in Turn 13.

items.title: Toto Wolff dismisses Helmut Marko's Russell theory: "He still has what it takes"
items.summary: Mercedes F1 boss Toto Wolff has dismissed suggestions from former Red Bull advisor Helmut Marko that there's no coming back for George Russell from being beaten to the world title by Kimi Antonelli. Antonelli is set to be crowned in the upcoming Mexico City Grand Prix barring exceptional circumstances delaying his coronation by one week.

items.title: Fred Vasseur reveals two costly moments that denied Ferrari US GP double podium
items.summary: The United States Grand Prix was a wildly successful weekend for Ferrari, if you strictly go off the timing sheets. The newly upgraded car possessed blazing-fast race pace, tyre degradation was fully under control, and Charles Leclerc dragged his machine to a brilliant second-place finish behind Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli.

items.title: Red Bull reveals damage behind Max Verstappen's US GP struggles
items.summary: When your star driver gets out of the car after grabbing a podium and immediately tells the global broadcast that the pitstops, tyres, and engine braking were all complete garbage, it is up to the team principal to jump on the nearest microphone and put out the fire.

items.title: David Coulthard rejects F1 regulation excuses with Ayrton Senna and Michael Schumacher comparison
items.summary: Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard has dismissed the narrative that drivers can blame poor performance on the championship's new 2026 regulations, insisting the all-time greats successfully adapt to any machinery. F1 introduced a major regulation change in 2026.

items.title: George Russell's Mercedes F1 future discussed amid Kimi Antonelli's success
items.summary: George Russell's long-term future at Mercedes has been questioned following the United States Grand Prix. Russell entered the 2026 Formula 1 season as one of the favourites for the title. But after winning the season-opening Australian Grand Prix and the Chinese sprint race, the Briton watched as his team-mate Kimi Antonelli became the youngest driver to lead the championship.
